metadata.case_name: CHEUNG YUEN FAN SALLY v. THE HONG KONG UNIVERSITY OF SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY

injuries.description: right postero-lateral disc prolapse at C3-4 with narrowing of the cervical canal
source: MRI taken of the cervical spine showed reversal of lordosis at C3-4 where there was a right postero-lateral disc prolapse with narrowing of the cervical canal.

injuries.description: chronic regional pain syndrome involving the right side of her body
source: By June of 2000, the plaintiff was diagnosed as having chronic regional pain syndrome involving the right side of her body.

injuries.description: right wrist tendonitis / sprained right wrist
source: diagnosed as suffering from right wrist tendonitis.
found to be suffering from right wrist tendonitis and was given anti-inflammatory medication.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of unspecified muscle, fascia or tendon at wrist or hand level

manifestations.description: pain, swelling and redness in her right wrist
limited movement of right shoulder and right wrist with diffuse tenderness
on and off swelling and temperature fluctuation of right upper limb
gross restriction of neck motion, with right arm pain during neck extension especially combined with right rotation
pain spread to the right side of the neck, shoulder, arm, forearm and hand

treatments_received: four injections between 26 February and 14 March 2000
treatment at United Christian Hospital�s Orthopaedic and Traumatology Department
admission into Hong Kong Sanatorium & Hospital in mid June 2000 treated with analgesic and anti-inflammatory agents
physiotherapy at MacLehose Medical Rehabilitation Centre for five months (Oct 2000 to Feb 2001)
referral to the Pain Team and the Department of Orthopaedic and Traumatology of Queen Mary Hospital
psychological treatment by clinical psychologist Wong Ting (QMH) from 27 November 2002 until 8 December 2004
treatments_future: conservative chiropractic treatments at least once per week for six months (medium term) and long term chiropractic treatment at least twice per month as maintenance (as advised by Dr Leung)
